title: Knowledge Check 7 - Lessons 31-35
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 31-35 - AI Agents. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: You must ensure a risky action cannot be called until a validation passes. Which mechanism do you use?
options: A longer, more forceful prompt instruction
A knowledge retriever on the action
An available when condition on the action that is false until the controlling variable is set
A second model call to check the state
questions.explanation: An available when condition is a platform gate that removes the action from the tool list until the variable is true, whereas a prompt instruction is only a suggestion the model may ignore.

questions.question: Which syntax resolves a variable or an action into content inside a prompt instruction?
options: A template expression with braces and a leading exclamation, such as a reference to a promotion product variable
A double-slash expression
An angle-bracket percent expression
A dollar-sign expression
questions.explanation: Template expressions use braces with a leading exclamation to resolve a variable or resource into the prompt, which is the agent's merge-field mechanism and is resolved before the prompt is assembled.

questions.question: What must be true of any variable that controls an available when gate?
options: The model sets it fresh on every turn
It must be a string type
It must be declared linked to an external source
It must have a deterministic code path that sets it, rather than relying on the model
questions.explanation: A gate variable must be set by code, in before_reasoning or through a run and set sequence, because a variable the model may or may not set makes the gate as random as the model.

questions.question: A requirement says the transfer action must be impossible to call until every validation passes. Which mechanism delivers that guarantee?
options: A prompt line telling the model to wait
A variable holding a note about the state
A template expression showing the balance
An available when filter on the action that stays false until the gating variable is set
questions.explanation: Only an available when clause removes the action from the model's tool list until the gating variable is true, whereas prompt wording and an ungated variable note can both be bypassed.

questions.question: A customer's verified id must survive into a later subagent so the agent does not re-ask. What is the correct mechanism?
options: The model's context memory
A variable set deterministically and read in later logic instructions
A template expression in the first subagent's prompt
A knowledge retriever on the customer record
questions.explanation: Context memory is not guaranteed across turns or subagents, so the fact belongs in a variable set by code and read later, which is what makes the cross-subagent reuse reliable.

questions.question: The reply must name the exact product the script already determined for the customer. Which mechanism do you use?
options: A template expression such as a reference to a promotion product variable in the prompt
Asking the model to look the product up in the prompt
An available when filter on the product action
A second gate variable to hold the product id
questions.explanation: A template expression renders the value the script already established, keeping the answer grounded, while asking the model to look it up routes a known fact back through the model and reopens the variability.

questions.question: A team wants the agent to handle order status and returns reliably, and the standard topics are too broad. What does Salesforce recommend?
options: Replace the broad standard topic with purpose-built custom topics that have narrow classification descriptions
Keep one broad standard topic and add more actions to it
Put the routing rules in topic instructions
Remove the classification description so the agent infers the job
questions.explanation: Salesforce states that narrow, clearly described topics classify more reliably than a catch-all, so specific custom topics beat a broad standard topic for this need.

questions.question: Where should a business rule that must always behave the same way live?
options: In the topic instructions
In the action's own Flow or Apex logic
In the classification description
In the agent's welcome message
questions.explanation: Topic and action instructions are non-deterministic, so deterministic or sensitive rules belong inside the action's Flow or Apex, where they always execute the same way.

questions.question: Two admins can both open an agent, but only one can run one of its custom actions. What explains this?
options: Custom actions are randomly assigned per user
The action is hidden until the agent is activated
A custom action inherits the access of the Flow, Apex class, or prompt template it references
Standard actions are required before custom actions run
questions.explanation: Access to a custom action depends on the asset behind it, so permission to the referenced Flow or Apex determines who can invoke the action.

questions.question: An agent keeps firing Get Task Details when the user wants project information. Both actions exist in the same topic. What is the best fix?
options: Remove the project action from the topic
Rename the actions so their verbs and descriptions clearly separate what each does
Move both actions into topic instructions
Add a validation rule on the Task object
questions.explanation: The model separates actions largely by name and description, so distinct, verb-led names and clear descriptions resolve the confusion better than removing the action.

questions.question: A request lands in no topic at all. Which part of the configuration is the first suspect?
options: The action's Apex class
The topic's action list
The set of classification descriptions, for a job nobody clearly owns
The feedback survey
questions.explanation: Routing into a topic runs on the classification description, so a request that reaches no topic usually means no description clearly covers that job.

questions.question: A custom standard action does everything the job needs and already fits the object. What should you do?
options: Build a custom action anyway to keep control
Remove the topic so the agent can act freely
Move the logic into topic instructions
Reuse the standard action, because it already serves the job
questions.explanation: A standard action that already fits the job should be reused, since a custom build adds maintenance and inherits its own access without adding value here.

questions.question: A team wants its internal staff to work with the agent inside their collaboration tool. Which connection and agent type fit?
options: The messaging connection on a service agent
The service email connection on a service agent
The Slack connection on an Employee agent
The telephony connection on a service agent
questions.explanation: Slack is an employee surface, and the Slack connection attaches to an Agentforce Employee agent, so it is the match for internal collaboration.

questions.question: You add a telephony connection so customers can call the agent. What must the agent support?
options: That it is voice-enabled through Agentforce Voice with a telephony provider selected
That it uses Enhanced Web Chat response formats
That it routes through Email-to-Case
That it runs only in the Agentforce panel
questions.explanation: Telephony connections route calls through Agentforce Voice to a voice-enabled agent, which requires selecting a telephony provider rather than any text-channel setup.

questions.question: Which connection routes a customer's inbound email to the agent for an autonomous response?
options: Enhanced Web Chat
The Slack connection
The Agentforce panel
The service email connection, which routes through Email-to-Case
questions.explanation: The service email connection routes through Email-to-Case so the service agent can respond to customer email, unlike the web and collaboration surfaces.
